symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: When the game state is Running or MainMenu (or Idling/Paused while an engine flag at gEngine+0x40 is set), the system places every active camera spline for this frame's time, then finishes and drops every active spline whose ended byte (+0x48 of its 0x50-byte record) is set. Inside the same gate it then runs ProcessScreenFade; outside those game states nothing of this runs.

does.text: Finishing an active spline does nothing at all unless the spline's byte +0x49 is set. With it set, it ends a splitscreen spline request if one was started, and - only while no loading screen is visible - restores the player's HUD, reopens the dialog UI if the player's character carries character flag 0x40, and, when the spline's fade time (+0x44) is above zero, queues a screen-fade request for that player in a map keyed by player id, with both of its flags set (fade-to and clear) and the fade time; it then puts the previous camera target back. DeactivateSlow (by spline name) marks a spline ended and finishes it at once.

does.check: not checkable live: the queued request lives in the system's own map, not in a component; its outcome is the next claim.
does.review: Review 2026-11-14 (Opus): corrected: byte +0x49 guards the whole of Finish (its if opens at the top and closes at the end of the function), not only the fade; the fade-time test sits inside the 'loading screen not visible' block, so no fade is queued while a loading screen shows.

does.text: If fade requests are queued, the system takes the carrier entity of last frame's requests or creates a new one, and for each queued player: with the fade-to flag it adds ecl::camera_spline::ScreenFadeToRequestManualOneFrameComponent (when not yet there) and puts into its Requests map, under the player id, a fresh creation record with a newly generated Guid; with the clear flag it adds ecl::camera_spline::ClearScreenFadeRequestManualOneFrameComponent (when not yet there) and appends to its Requests a record with a Guid. The queue is emptied afterwards. Both types are read by ecl::screen_fade::ScreenFadeSystem (ProcessScreenFadeToRequests, ProcessClearScreenFadeRequests). So both appear, client side, the frame a camera spline started with a fade time (Osiris StartCameraSpline's FadeTime) is finished, if the spline's byte +0x49 is set and no loading screen is visible.

does.proposed_recipe: camera_spline_fade_finish (PROPOSED): GustavX:WLD_Main_A from the checkpoint; server: find a spline of the level (an entity with ls::SplineComponent, its GUID), then Osi.StartCameraSpline(spline, Osi.GetHostCharacter(), 1.0, 1, 0, 0); sleep 3; Osi.StopCameraSpline(spline, Osi.GetHostCharacter()); sleep 2. Untested: that FadeTime lands in +0x44, that StopCameraSpline reaches Finish, and what sets byte +0x49.

How StopCameraSpline / the server reach Deactivate/DeactivateSlow or the ended byte on the client (the server's esv::CameraSplineSystem was not read).
What gEngine+0x40 is (it lets splines play while the game is idling or paused).
sure: yes for the creation of both fade request types and the carrier's destruction (adders resolved); no for the play path to Finish with a fade (the +0x49/+0x44 origins are not read)
